site.title: Cooperage Brewing
site.tagline: Brewery and taproom in Smithfield, Dublin 7

categories.name: Beers
categories.description: The core range and the specials.

posts.title: Haymarket
posts.content: Our first beer and still the one we sell most of. Soft, orangey, dry at the end.
posts.excerpt: Pale ale, 4.6%. The one most people start with.

posts.title: Arran Quay
posts.content: White grape and lime from the Nelson. Brewed every six weeks, gone in four.
posts.excerpt: IPA, 6.2%. White grape and lime from the Nelson.

posts.title: Bow Street
posts.content: Roast, cocoa and a little lactose to round it off. On nitro on Sundays.
posts.excerpt: Stout, 5.0%. Roast, cocoa and a little lactose.

posts.title: Phoenix
posts.content: Six weeks of lagering at one degree. Crisp, bready, a little floral.

posts.title: Stoneybatter
posts.content: A light, hoppy beer for the second half of a long afternoon.

posts.title: Four Courts
posts.content: Eleven months in a Jamaican rum barrel. Poured in thirds only, and only in winter.
posts.excerpt: Imperial stout, 10.5%. Rum barrel, thirds only.

posts.title: Pub quiz, Wednesday 7 October
posts.content:
Teams of up to six, €2 each, cash prize and a bar tab for the winners. Starts 20:00; Síle asks the questions and takes no appeals.

Book a table if you are more than five.

posts.title: Launch: Red Cow raspberry sour, Friday 2 October
posts.content: Our first sour in two years goes on line 7 at 17:00, and cans go on sale at the same time. Limit four cans a person until Sunday.

posts.title: Tasting with the brewers, Sunday 4 October
posts.content:
Six thirds, one of each core beer and two from the tanks, with Aoife talking you through them. 14:00, €22, twelve places.

Email to book a place

posts.title: Tap takeover: Hazel Row from Wexford, Friday 9 October
posts.content: Four lines of Hazel Row Brewing on Friday from 16:00. Our own beers stay on the other four.

posts.title: Canning day, and why the Pilsner runs out
posts.content: Phoenix sits in the tank for six weeks before we can it. When it sells faster than that, it runs out. We are adding a tank in November.

posts.title: Hop harvest brew with fresh Irish hops
posts.content: We drove to a farm in Kilkenny on Tuesday morning and had the hops in the kettle by 15:00. The beer is on in three weeks.
